title: What the Score Measured: Failure Attribution in an Agent Memory Evaluation

citation.apa: Vitale, D., & Guo, B. (2026). What the score measured: Failure attribution in an agent memory evaluation [Public preprint]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22980060
citation.chicago: Vitale, Dino, and Baixin Guo. "What the Score Measured: Failure Attribution in an Agent Memory Evaluation." Public preprint. Zenodo, 2026. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22980060.
citation.mla: Vitale, Dino, and Baixin Guo. What the Score Measured: Failure Attribution in an Agent Memory Evaluation. Public preprint, Zenodo, 2026, doi:10.5281/zenodo.22980060.

abstract: This public preprint, co-authored with Dino Vitale (Boundary Labs), documents why an outcome score alone cannot identify which component of a LongMemEval-based agent memory evaluation failed. It separates observed outcomes, available evidence, failure attribution, and judge confidence, and shows how missing traces limit what a failed answer can tell us about the memory system. The reconstruction, harness repair, rerun and write-up are Dino Vitale's; the audit of public materials, the attribution rubric, the test matrix and the judging protocol are Baixin Guo's. The instrument itself is deposited separately as a standalone methods report (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23273896), so both records describe one study rather than two unrelated ones. Its four-rater blind protocol was applied to 150 predictions, which are 25 cases scored under six conditions rather than 150 distinct questions. It is a preprint, not a peer-reviewed publication.
